claims.statement: Official BZP and TED feeds expose published notices and deadlines, creating a recurring observable decision event; the actual labor loss per bad bid is not established by these sources.
The proposed payer is the SME sales owner who allocates bid labor; willingness to pay 499-1499 PLN monthly instead of using portals or consultants is unverified.

TED says its search API permits anonymous retrieval for reuse, and Poland's BZP integration page says notice reading does not require an integration procedure; the founder can own the independently written scoring layer while keeping source rights separate.
Official data access is nonexclusive and can change under published terms, so defensibility must come from workflow fit and consented outcome labels rather than raw notice access.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Owner, sales director, or bid manager
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: A decision log tied to client eligibility, margin, and historical outcomes must outperform generic notice alerts
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Founder company owns direct SME subscriptions
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Narrow-sector outbound, procurement consultants, trade groups, and accountants

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Founder-led demonstrations and partner referral fees; target under four months of gross profit
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Monthly advance subscription or discounted annual prepayment
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Target 75-90% after a vertical template stabilizes; unvalidated
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Vertical rule calibration, source-link QA, onboarding, and user support
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Terms monitoring, security, professional disclaimers, and procurement-law review
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 499-1499 PLN per month by monitored categories and users, plus onboarding
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Notice ingestion, OCR, model calls, alerts, and document storage

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Tender portals and procurement consultancies can add AI summaries, scoring, or bundled alert services
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Every published matching notice triggers a go/no-go decision; loss is bid-preparation labor spent on ineligible or low-fit tenders and opportunity cost from missed viable notices
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Tender volume exceeds manual scanning capacity, a bid is disqualified on a detectable requirement, or a deadline is missed

contrary_evidence: TED explicitly describes commercial organisations integrating its data into added-value platforms, signaling low raw-data scarcity.
Public portals already provide search and filtering, and consultants may bundle bid selection with preparation.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Independent creation with copyright ownership and trade-secret protection for code and derived nonpublic features
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Use the alternate official notice API and client-uploaded tender documents; never represent public data as exclusive
critical_control_point.current_owner: Founder company owns independently created code and derived rules; public authorities retain source notices
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Founder company owns direct SME subscriptions
critical_control_point.duration: Indefinite while maintained; public input rights remain governed separately
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder can independently create and own the scoring software; TED and BZP offer published access paths to notices, but neither public dataset becomes founder-owned.
critical_control_point.renewal: not applicable to owned code; API and client agreements reviewed annually
critical_control_point.subject: Independently created bid-fit model, rule library, and decision-log software

economics.acquisition_route: Narrow vertical outbound, consultant referrals, associations, and outcome-tracked trials
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, not forecast: 1500 customers at 850 PLN monthly imply 15.3m PLN annual recurring revenue; low churn and repeatable vertical expansion would be required for a 5m PLN founder outcome
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours daily for one vertical; avoid bespoke bid writing that would turn it into an agency
economics.gross_margin_basis: Automated official-feed ingestion and scoring reused across customers in one vertical
economics.payback: Target under four months of account gross profit; unvalidated
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 499-1499 PLN monthly plus 500-2000 PLN vertical onboarding
economics.retention_or_repeat: Renews while relevant tenders recur and the decision log saves demonstrable bid hours or finds wins

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Client-consented bid/no-bid decisions and outcomes improve vertical-specific fit features and calibration
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs that repeatedly bid for public-sector contracts in a narrow technical category
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct vertical outreach and nonexclusive referrals from procurement consultants, accountants, and trade associations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Specialist bid-fit scoring, cited requirement extraction, decision log, and outcome learning; final legal and commercial judgment remains human
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Sales owner pays a monthly subscription for monitored categories, decision briefs, and deadline alerts
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new notice appears and a small team must rapidly decide whether qualification, geography, margin, and deadline justify bid work

founder_fit: Natural-language extraction, scoring calibration, and outcome analysis match data-science skills
The product serves a measurable recurring decision rather than requiring public audience building
Official APIs allow inexpensive asynchronous prototyping
Vertical templates and self-service onboarding can constrain founder time below five hours daily
risks: A bad no-go recommendation can cost a customer a material opportunity
Source schema or access terms can change
Users may mistake extracted requirements for legal advice
Generic AI features could commoditize summaries quickly

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical software subscription for pre-bid decisions
structure.control_point: Founder-owned scoring code and decision record at the point before bid resources are committed
structure.critical_dependency: Continuing lawful access to complete public-notice data and client feedback

thesis: Own a Polish-language bid-fit scoring and evidence engine built on openly reusable BZP and TED notices, then sell specialized SMEs a daily go/no-go checkpoint before expensive bid preparation begins.
title: Public-Tender Bid-Cost Gate
uncertainties: Which vertical has enough tender frequency and bid cost
Availability of award and participation outcomes needed for calibration
Whether procurement documents can be reliably parsed across formats and languages
